extractor.note: Read every paragraph carrying transcend- (outside transcendental), immanen-, surpass or overstep, in file order. No stratum is set: the commentary follows the composite main text and does not assign its sections to the 1920/21, 1923 or 1925/26 deliveries.

coverage_note: Term-led pass over the whole file (lines 1-834): every paragraph containing the transcendence family, including bare transcendent and immanent, was read; paragraphs without such a word were not read.

units.claim: Through remembering, consciousness becomes an object for itself, so that time-consciousness becomes its own first transcendence.
units.quote: First, through remembering, consciousness becomes an object for itself—time-consciousness becomes its own first transcendence.

units.claim: Perception has its intentional object immanently as an inseparable sense, which has immanent being even if the perception is deceptive; the perceived tree as such is a purely immanent object, not a thing in nature.
units.quote: If we judge this sense, we judge something demonstrable in an evident manner—having immanent being even if the perception turns out to be deceptive.

units.claim: The principle of inadequacy applies to transcendent perception: the given is always a partial self-presentation of a fuller object exceeding any single act.
units.quote: This is the Husserlian principle of inadequacy applied to transcendent perception: the given is always a partial self-presentation of a fuller object that exceeds any single perceptual act.

units.claim: A non-intuitive pointing beyond makes the seen side a mere side, so that something transcending the side is intended as perceived.
units.quote: What characterizes the actually seen side as a mere side is a non-intuitive pointing beyond or indicating—what provides for the fact that the side is not taken for the thing, but that something transcending the side is intended as perceived.

units.claim: The possibility of renewed perception of the transcendent is the fundamental trait of transcendent perception, through which alone an abiding world is there for us.
units.quote: That a renewed perception is possible for transcendence characterizes the fundamental trait of transcendent perception: through it alone, an abiding world is there for us, a reality that can be pregiven and freely at our disposal.

units.claim: An immanent object has only one way of being given in each Now, so the concept of appearance takes on a new and unique sense for the transcendent object.
units.quote: The concept of appearance thus has a new and unique sense for the transcendent object.

units.claim: A transcendent object can be constituted only when an immanent content is constituted as substratum and takes on the function of adumbration.
units.quote: a transcendent object like a thing can only be constituted when an immanent content is constituted as substratum—this immanent content is substituted for the function of "adumbration," of exhibiting appearance

units.claim: Husserl calls apperception the accomplishment of bestowing on immanent sensible data the function of exhibiting something transcendent; for transcendent objects esse is in principle distinguished from percipi.
units.quote: Husserl characterizes consciousness's accomplishment of bestowing on mere immanent sensible data the function of exhibiting something objectively "transcendent" as apperception.

units.claim: Treating inadequation as a haphazard lack that a higher intellect could overcome is called totally preposterous; a spatial object cannot be given through immanent perception.
units.quote: The talk of inadequation as a haphazard lack that a higher intellect could overcome is "totally preposterous."

units.claim: Perception constitutes immanent objects in their absoluteness, not by constant sense-modification in the sense of approximation.
units.quote: For immanent objects the situation is entirely different: perception constitutes them in their absoluteness; they are not constituted by constant sense-modification in the sense of approximation.

units.claim: For the transcendent world there are prefigurings and corroborated experiential belief, yet further experience could in principle continue contrary to all expectations.
units.quote: For the transcendent world: there are prefigurings for further experiences, motivated experiential belief corroborated through innumerable accordances—but in the final analysis, is it not possible for further experience to continue contrary to all expectations?

units.claim: Immanently constituted being in its living present is self-giving and essentially incapable of being crossed out, though deception in remembering is raised for the immanent sphere.
units.quote: Immanently constituted being in its living present is not only self-giving but essentially incapable of being crossed out.

units.claim: Space as a principle of individuation for transcendent objects is transposed to the immanent sphere, where every immanent temporal object has its temporal shape.
units.quote: This connects directly to Husserl's analyses in Thing and Space (Hua XVI) of space as a principle of individuation for transcendent objects, here transposed to the immanent sphere.

units.claim: Rememberings arise in the immanence of the present, but what they presentify is transcendent to it; the entire past of consciousness is given transcendently.
units.quote: Our entire past of consciousness is given transcendently.

units.claim: The stream of consciousness is the first transcendent, the transcendent self instituted in the streaming present and coming to incomplete self-giving in rememberings.
units.quote: The stream of consciousness is the first transcendent in the manner of a primordial source—the transcendent self primordially instituted in the streaming present, issuing in self-giving and verification through rememberings.

units.claim: The immanent stream determines the future by constituting within itself an objective world in a transcendent intentionality; things are constituted in lived-experiences but not as lived-experiences.
units.quote: Through the fact that it constitutes within itself an objective world in a transcendent intentionality.

absences.expected_because: Rememberings as source of the in-itself are what §45 describes as the transcendent giving of the past, and §24 had posed the in-itself problem for the immanent sphere.
Conflict of rememberings bears on the true being of the immanent past that the next chapter treats as primordially transcendent.
